items.headline: Amazon deforestation falls to its lowest level in a decade
items.summary: Brazil's national space research institute reported that forest clearing in the Brazilian Amazon dropped sharply in the first half of twenty twenty six compared to the same period last year, marking the smallest six month loss in ten years. Officials credited stepped up enforcement and government policy for the improvement, though researchers cautioned that fires and illegal mining remain ongoing threats.
items.why_it_matters: Less rainforest destruction means fewer greenhouse gas emissions and better odds of preserving one of the planet's most important carbon sinks and biodiversity reservoirs.
items.source_name: Al Jazeera, citing Brazil's National Institute for Space Research
